findings.description: Runtime discovery resolves `tools/sandbox-runtime` relative to "the dispatcher's own Git top-level" (design.md:123-125), but the installed runtime is an `npm ci` output under `tools/sandbox-runtime/node_modules` that wp-runtime gitignores (work-packages.yaml:81, 98). Every mutating skill runs from a managed linked worktree (AGENTS.md), and runtime skill copies live under `<worktree>/.claude/skills/` (untracked; `git ls-files .claude/skills/shared` is empty). `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` from that dispatcher returns the worktree, where `node_modules` never exists because `git worktree add` carries no ignored files. Discovery therefore reports 'unavailable' in the normal execution model and every sandbox decision takes the fail-open path; enforcement would only apply from the shared checkout, which mutating skills may not use. Specify a rung that survives linked worktrees: parent of `git rev-parse --git-common-dir` (as `_main_repo_from_cwd` already does, review_dispatcher.py:2373-2407) or a per-user XDG data install, and run the capable-host evidence from a linked worktree.
findings.resolution: Add a linked-worktree-aware discovery rung to D7 and task 3.2; make the evidence job execute from a `.git-worktrees/` checkout.

findings.description: D4 renders an unavailable policy snapshot as deny-all and launches (design.md:78-79; agent-coordinator spec.md:26-30). D8 and the poll scenario protect only against a pre-launch denial (design.md:145-148; vendor-dispatch spec.md:112-116). During a coordinator outage the poll command is launched inside SRT with no egress, exits nonzero after start, and `poll_for_result` treats nonzero exit as terminal and closes the completion ledger (review_dispatcher.py:1703-1719). The 'Poll enforcement failure does not abandon remote work' scenario cannot be met for the most likely failure (policy outage). Classify an outage-derived deny-all snapshot as a pre-launch retryable condition for submission-scope polls; keep authored deny-all fail-closed.
findings.resolution: Add to D8 and the spec that an unavailable export at poll time returns a retryable pre-launch denial; add a RED test for outage-during-poll.

findings.description: Audit persistence failure SHALL fail closed (vendor-dispatch spec.md:97-98; design.md:110-111), but nothing states that sandbox events are emitted only when `requested_isolation=sandbox`; the event schema allows `none`/`worktree` (sandbox-execution-event.schema.json:36). An implementer emitting one event per launch adds a coordinator round-trip to every non-sandbox dispatch and, when coordinator and outbox both fail, blocks plain review dispatch that today never contacts the coordinator, contradicting 'Non-sandbox behavior remains compatible' (spec.md:17-21) and the byte-compatible rollback (proposal.md:130-131).
findings.resolution: State in D6 and the compatibility scenario that no event, export call, or outbox write occurs when effective isolation is none or worktree.

findings.description: The outbox drains oldest-first and removes an entry only after acknowledgement (design.md:114-116), but the plan never distinguishes transient failures (network, 503 per openapi.yaml:67) from permanent rejections (401/403/422 per openapi.yaml:64-66). One entry the coordinator will never accept (trust below 3 for the target lane, schema drift, stale agent_id) blocks every later entry forever while new launches keep 'succeeding' via outbox writes, degrading durability to a local file. It is also unstated whether a 4xx on the live attempt may use the outbox; treating 403 as unavailable lets a low-trust host run unsandboxed fallbacks indefinitely with only local evidence.
findings.resolution: 5xx/connection errors qualify for outbox fallback; 4xx fails closed live; during drain a 4xx dead-letters the entry without blocking newer ones; warn on dead-letter count.

findings.description: The routed path is narrower than D1 implies. The roadmap host dispatches by invoking `/implement-feature` and `/validate-feature` through SKILL.md (autopilot-roadmap/SKILL.md:189-190); `dispatch_phase` has no production caller besides the smoke script (smoke_provider_dispatch.py:200). Claude Code lanes run as in-harness Agent-tool sub-agents, and `codex-remote`/`grok-remote` already declare `isolation: sandbox` with no CLI section (agents.yaml:179-206, 326-348). None of these pass through the backend, so a `sandbox` decision for them is neither enforced nor recorded as `applied=false`, violating 'Execution metadata is truthful' (vendor-dispatch spec.md:88-92) for most real dispatches. State who records `applied=false` with a reason such as `backend_not_applicable` for non-CLI sinks, or that the router never assigns sandbox to lanes without a CLI backend.
findings.resolution: Add to D1/task 4.3 a host-emitted degraded event for Agent-tool/SDK/cloud lanes carrying a sandbox decision, or a router constraint.

findings.description: D5 builds 'a minimal trusted PATH from their parent directories' of Node, SRT, bwrap, socat, and rg (design.md:98-100), and SRT forwards the environment to the child. Write-capable modes (`codex exec -s workspace-write`, `claude --allowedTools ... Bash`, agents.yaml:129, 172-174) shell out to `git`, `bash`, `python3`, `gh`, `uv`, and test runners; with `/usr/bin` and `/usr/local/bin` absent every alternative/quick dispatch fails inside the sandbox for a reason unrelated to policy. Define PATH explicitly: runtime binary parents plus a fixed system allowlist plus original absolute, non-user-writable entries.
findings.resolution: Amend D5 and task 3.3 with the PATH policy; add a test that `git --version` runs under the sandboxed environment.

findings.description: D3 redirects HOME/XDG to a per-launch ephemeral root and treats credentials as read-only inputs (design.md:50-55, 98-101) but never says how a vendor CLI finds them once HOME moves. SRT has no bind mounts (upstream README: only read/write allow/deny on the real filesystem), so the two possible mechanisms differ materially: pointing a vendor config-dir variable at the real directory requires it to be writable (claude writes `~/.claude/projects`, codex writes `~/.codex/sessions`); copying the credential file into the ephemeral root breaks OAuth refresh-token rotation, since claude and codex rewrite their credential file on refresh and a token rotated inside a discarded copy invalidates the operator's real credential. Task 5.1 requires only that a real vendor 'enters the backend' (tasks.md:46-49), so this is never exercised before rollout.
findings.resolution: Specify the per-vendor mechanism and agents.yaml fields in D3/D5 and task 4.1; require the capable-host evidence to include one successful authenticated vendor call.

findings.description: The upstream SRT README states that on Linux the sandboxed process has no network namespace, all traffic must go through the host proxies via `HTTP_PROXY`/`HTTPS_PROXY`, and this 'may be ignored by programs that don't respect these variables'. Node's built-in fetch (undici) does not honor those variables by default, and `pi` and the autopilot `local` provider are Node programs. D4's rollout precondition is an endpoint inventory plus a no-op preflight (design.md:83-86), so a lane whose CLI ignores proxy variables passes both gates and then loses all egress under `sandbox`.
findings.resolution: Add per-vendor proxy-awareness to the task 5.3 inventory and the evidence record; make the task 5.1 'allowed egress succeeds' probe use the same HTTP client class as the vendor being rolled out.

findings.description: The canonical capable runner is `macos-14` (design.md:168-169; tasks.md:51-52), which exercises only the Seatbelt backend. The Linux preflight and bubblewrap path in D7 (design.md:129-133) are what every operator host here uses, yet they are validated only by mocked unit tests. The upstream README documents the Ubuntu 24.04 remedy (`kernel.apparmor_restrict_unprivileged_userns` disabled) and GitHub Ubuntu runners permit `sudo sysctl`, so a Linux evidence job is feasible. Either add an `ubuntu-24.04` leg with the sysctl step and require a Linux pass before rolling out Linux lanes, or state that Linux enforcement is unproven at landing and encode platform in the evidence so the roadmap gate cannot mistake a macOS pass for Linux coverage.
findings.resolution: Add a Linux matrix leg to `.github/workflows/sandbox-runtime.yml`, or give `verify_sandbox_runtime_evidence.py` a required-platform argument.

findings.description: wp-validation-docs passes when `verify_sandbox_runtime_evidence.py` accepts a checked-in JSON file (work-packages.yaml:205-213); design.md:169-172 says the record 'includes workflow/run identity' but never says the verifier checks it against GitHub. A validator agent that cannot trigger or wait for the manual workflow can satisfy the gate by writing a plausible file, the 'manufactured pass' D7 forbids (design.md:132-133). The plan also omits how the validator obtains the artifact (`gh workflow run ... --ref <branch>` then `gh run download`).
findings.resolution: Task 5.2: verifier confirms run id, head SHA, workflow file, and `conclusion=success` via `gh run view --json`, fails closed offline; document the trigger/download commands.

findings.description: The quality-gate step runs Ruff and `openspec validate` only (work-packages.yaml:220-225; tasks.md:55-56), but CI runs `mypy src/` under `strict = true` for agent-coordinator (.github/workflows/ci.yml:73-74; agent-coordinator/pyproject.toml:173-175) and `install.sh --check` plus the dependency-direction linter after a fresh install (ci.yml:103-107). wp-policy-audit adds coordinator code and wp-runtime adds new `skills/shared/*.py` modules that install sync must know about (worktree.py:34-35; skills/install-manifest.json). Neither gate is in any package verification, so the branch can be green locally and fail CI.
findings.resolution: Add `mypy src/` for agent-coordinator and `bash skills/install.sh --check` (after registering new shared modules in the manifest) to the wp-validation-docs gate and task 5.4.

findings.description: The execution context permits `location: null` (dispatch-execution-context.schema.json:23) for standalone lanes, but the derived event requires `location` in `local|cloud` with no null (sandbox-execution-event.schema.json:33). No mapping rule exists, so a standalone dispatch for a lane whose agents.yaml entry omits `location` cannot produce a schema-valid event and would fail closed on the audit step.
findings.resolution: Make context `location` non-null (default `local` for CLI lanes at the adapter boundary) or allow null in the event schema; state the rule in D1.

findings.description: D3 requires the root to equal `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` and to pass the `checkout_policy.py` managed-worktree check (design.md:55-57), while D8 lists the review snapshot fallback as covered (design.md:143). Snapshots are detached worktrees at `<main>/.git-worktrees/.review-snapshots/<round>/<vendor>` (review_dispatcher.py:2410-2430); for that path `_managed_worktree_root` returns `.git-worktrees/.review-snapshots` (checkout_policy.py:189-202), not the snapshot top-level. Whether 'pass the check' means `allowed=True` or `worktree_root == root` is unstated; under the strict reading every sandboxed snapshot retry fails closed.
findings.resolution: State the exact predicate and add a test that a `.review-snapshots` root is accepted for review mode.

findings.description: 'Rendering never widens policy' (agent-coordinator spec.md:20-24) is argued only from deny-first precedence. The SQL matcher treats `*.github.com` as `LIKE '%.github.com'`, which never matches the apex (009_network_policies.sql:85-88), and the upstream SRT README does not state whether `*.example.com` matches the apex. If SRT's wildcard is apex-inclusive, an authored `*.example.com` allow renders wider than the coordinator's own matcher, contradicting the scenario. Task 3.1 tests should pin the apex and multi-label semantics observed from SRT 0.0.77 and enforce the subset property or document the divergence.
findings.resolution: Add a capability-gated apex probe and a unit test asserting the renderer's match set is a subset of the SQL match set.

findings.description: Task 5.1 places the controlled vendor fixture 'under the runtime package' (tasks.md:46), while the only package allowed to write it puts it at `skills/shared/tests/fixtures/sandbox_vendor.py` (work-packages.yaml:94) and scopes itself to tasks 3.1-3.4 (work-packages.yaml:72). wp-validation-docs is described as 'Collect task 5.1 evidence' (work-packages.yaml:174) but cannot write under `skills/` (189-196). No package owns writing task 5.1, and the location contradiction will surface as a scope-check rejection during coordinated execution.
findings.resolution: Assign task 5.1 to wp-runtime explicitly and align tasks.md to the `skills/shared/tests/fixtures/` path.
